title: Top 3 FBR POS System Issues: A Troubleshooting Guide
metaDescription: FBR POS system issues like token expiry, offline sync failures, and QR errors — what causes them and the practical fixes that keep your IRIS integration compliant.
content:
What FBR POS system issues actually are

FBR POS system issues are the integration failures that stop a point-of-sale system from correctly reporting sales to the Federal Board of Revenue in real time. They include expired authentication tokens, invoices that never sync after an outage, QR codes that fail validation, and wrong tax-rate mapping. The danger is that most of them are silent — the counter keeps printing receipts while invoices quietly never reach FBR IRIS.

For any Tier-1 retailer in Pakistan, that silence is expensive. A business can run for weeks believing it is compliant, then receive a penalty notice because thousands of sales were never reported. Understanding the handful of issues that cause almost all of these failures is the fastest way to protect your STRN and avoid fines.

Why these issues happen in the first place

Almost every FBR POS problem traces back to one of three things: a broken assumption about how the IRIS API behaves, an unreliable internet connection at the point of sale, or configuration that drifted out of date. The FBR IRIS API is strict about authentication, timing, and tax calculation, and a POS that was set up once and never maintained will eventually fall out of step with it.

The most common FBR POS system issues

These five account for the overwhelming majority of real-world failures.

  • Token expiry — IRIS session tokens last about 60 minutes. A POS that caches the first token forever stops submitting after an hour, with no obvious error at the counter.
  • Offline sync failures — sales made during an internet outage must be queued and submitted later with their original timestamps. Many systems either drop them or resubmit with the wrong time.
  • QR / invoice validation errors — a receipt printed locally does not mean IRIS accepted it. If the submission failed, the QR will not validate on the FBR portal.
  • Incorrect tax-rate mapping — applying the standard rate to exempt or zero-rated items produces wrong submissions and over-charged customers, which triggers audits.
  • IRIS downtime and rate limits — at peak hours the IRIS endpoint can throttle high-volume businesses, rejecting submissions that are not retried with backoff.

How to diagnose a failed invoice submission

When a customer says their QR will not verify, or your monthly counts do not match, work through these steps in order:

  1. Open the IRIS dashboard and confirm whether the invoice actually exists there. If it does not, the submission failed — the receipt was printed locally only.
  2. Check the token age in your POS logs. If failures cluster after the first hour of a shift, you have a token-refresh problem.
  3. Inspect the offline queue. Count how many invoices are pending sync; a growing queue means the retry logic is stuck.
  4. Compare timestamps. If queued invoices submitted with the reconnection time rather than the sale time, fix the timestamp handling.
  5. Review the tax rates applied to the affected items against the current FBR schedule.
  6. Reconcile the totals — POS invoice count versus IRIS count for the period. The gap is your real error rate.

A real example: a Karachi pharmacy

A pharmacy in Saddar, Karachi passed its first week of FBR integration cleanly, then started getting customer complaints that QR codes would not verify. The owner assumed the printer was at fault. In reality the POS cached its IRIS token for the whole day, so every sale after roughly 11 a.m. failed silently. Around 60% of a day's invoices never reached FBR. Because the gap was caught during a monthly reconciliation rather than by an inspector, the business corrected the token-refresh setting and re-submitted the backlog — avoiding a penalty that, for that volume, would have run well past PKR 100,000.

Quick reference: issue, symptom, fix

IssueSymptomFix

Offline syncMissing invoices after outageQueue locally, submit with original timestamp
QR validationQR fails on FBR portalConfirm invoice exists in IRIS first
Tax mappingWrong tax on receiptsMap exempt/zero-rated items correctly
Rate limitsPeak-hour rejectionsRetry with exponential backoff

Common mistakes that make it worse

  • Trusting the printed receipt as proof of compliance instead of the IRIS dashboard.
  • Never reconciling — without a monthly POS-versus-IRIS count check, silent failures go unnoticed until an inspection.
  • Using software that has not been updated in a year — FBR rules and SROs change, and stale integrations break.
  • Ignoring the offline queue until it overflows, losing the original sale times.

How to prevent FBR POS issues for good

Prevention is mostly discipline. Choose a POS that refreshes its IRIS token automatically, queues offline sales with correct timestamps, and retries rate-limited submissions. Then build a habit of reconciling against the IRIS dashboard every month — see our FBR compliance checklist for the full routine. If you are still setting up, the IRIS portal registration guide walks through doing it right the first time, and our guide to generating valid FBR QR invoices covers the validation step that trips up most retailers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why does my FBR POS keep showing token expiry errors?

FBR IRIS authentication tokens expire roughly every 60 minutes. If your POS caches the first token and never refreshes it, every sale after the first hour silently fails. The fix is proactive refresh — request a new token about five minutes before expiry rather than waiting for a rejection.

What happens to sales made while the internet is down?

A correctly built POS queues those invoices locally and submits them to FBR IRIS when the connection returns, stamped with the original sale time. If your system batches them with the reconnection time instead, FBR's monitoring flags the timestamp mismatch as a discrepancy.

Why is the QR code on my invoice not validating on the FBR portal?

Usually because the invoice was never accepted by IRIS (a failed submission still prints a receipt locally) or the QR encodes the wrong invoice reference. Verify the invoice actually appears in your IRIS dashboard before trusting the printed QR.

Can FBR fine me for POS integration errors I did not notice?

Yes. Penalties start around PKR 10,000 and can reach PKR 1,000,000 for repeated violations, plus possible STRN suspension. Silent submission failures are the most dangerous because the business believes it is compliant while invoices never reach FBR.

How often should I reconcile my POS with the IRIS dashboard?

At least monthly, ideally weekly. Compare the invoice count your POS recorded against the count IRIS shows; any gap points to rejected or unsynced invoices you can fix before they become an audit problem.

The bottom line

Most FBR POS system issues come down to five fixable causes, and nearly all of them hide behind a normal-looking receipt. Treat the IRIS dashboard — not the printer — as your source of truth, reconcile every month, and keep your software current. Do that and the penalties that catch most Pakistani retailers simply never reach you.
